newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: TIBS 1997 outlook tough, but profits seen.
newsitem.headline: TIBS 1997 outlook tough, but profits seen.

text.p: Transportation group TIBS Holdings Ltd said on Monday it expected bus companies to be affected by high operating and depreciation costs but saw profits improving in 1997 after a cost reduction programme.
"The group will continue its efforts towards higher productivity and work improvement measures to reduce costs," TIBS said in its annual results statement.
TIBS said it was exploring all avenues to improve bus revenues, including fare adjustments.
The company reported a plunge into the red, recording a loss of Singapore $5.1 million for the year to December 31, 1996 against a S$6.9 million profit in the previous year.
The company said results had been hit by competition from Singapore's Mass Rapid Transit rail network, higher operational costs and lower margins.
The purchase of 384 new buses and higher manpower costs were the principal factors affecting bus operations, TIBS said.
Non-bus operations contributed less to turnover and were affected by continued weakness in their sectors.
"The non-bus companies, in particular manufacturing companies, are expected to continue to be affected by the weaker electronics industry and high production costs," the company said.
